increments.title: A correction round of pure coverage gaps runs test-author and reviewer only
increments.goal: Let the reviewer classify each finding it returns as a coverage gap or a defect, and have the workflow run a round whose findings are all coverage gaps through test-author and reviewer alone, visibly and on the record.
criteria: The reviewer's structured return carries a per-finding classification field that says whether the finding is a coverage gap or a defect; it is a value the reviewer sets, not a phrase the workflow greps out of prose.
When every finding of a round is classified a coverage gap, that correction round runs the test-author and the reviewer only, and does not run the researcher or the implementer.
A round with at least one finding classified a defect runs the full four-agent chain exactly as it does today.
The workflow log()s that it is correcting coverage only when it takes the shortened path.
The reviewer's classification of each finding is recorded in backlog.json alongside the round it belongs to.
The reviewer's own brief states what makes a finding a coverage gap rather than a defect, so the classification is decided the same way twice.
The test suite passes.
increments.note: Accepted at review round 2 with no findings: the per-finding kind enum, the coverage-only routing in both workflows, the log line, the recorded classification and the reviewer's stated rule are all pinned by test-repo.sh drivers w17/w18/w19 and a backlog recorder case; bash test-repo.sh 71 cases exit 0 and ./test.sh all 6 suites exit 0.

increments.title: The UI test harness returns null for an id the rendered markup does not contain
increments.goal: Stop the argus-ui test harness conjuring an element for every id, so an assertion that reads a container the page never rendered fails the way a browser would, and prove the harness with a case in the suite.
criteria: installFakes in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs resolves an id the rendered markup does not contain to null rather than to a created-and-cached fake element.

Every existing case in the suite still passes, or is corrected to assert what the page actually renders; the report says which cases were corrected and why each was passing against markup the page never wrote.

A case in the suite proves the harness itself: it removes a container from the rendered markup and shows at least one assertion going red as a result, so the guard is part of the run rather than a manual mutation check.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test passes, with the case count reported.

## What the tree actually holds (read this before anything else)

The criteria name `installFakes` in `tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs`. **Neither the function nor the file exists in this branch.** Commit `1c94c20` ("The timeline is the interface…", PR #65) landed the timeline work as a squash that replaced the old `app.test.mjs` with `page.test.mjs`, `context.test.mjs` and `timeline.test.mjs`. A repo-wide grep for `installFakes` finds it only in this issue's own `issue.md` and `backlog.json`; a repo-wide grep for `getElementById` finds it only in `public/app.js` and in one string literal inside `page.test.mjs`. So today the argus-ui suite has **no DOM harness at all**: `page.test.mjs` asserts on the *source text* of `app.js` with regexes, and `context.test.mjs` / `timeline.test.mjs` assert on the HTML strings the pure modules return. `public/app.js` — the only file that touches `document` — is never executed by any test.

Two consequences, both of which the implementer must carry into the report:

1. The increment **creates** the harness with the null contract built in, rather than repairing a conjuring one. The criterion is satisfied by `installFakes` existing in `test/app.test.mjs` and resolving an unrendered id to `null`.
2. Criterion 2 ("every existing case still passes, or is corrected") has the answer **"no case was corrected, and here is why"**: no case in the suite was ever backed by a DOM harness, so no assertion in it could have been passing against markup the page never wrote. The report must state that, name commit `1c94c20` as where the old harness went, and confirm the six existing files are untouched.

Do not treat the increment as moot. The trap's second half — that nothing runs `app.js` against a document at all, so the containers it reads by id are pinned by nothing — is live, and the work below closes it.

## What gets built

One new file, `tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs`, holding the harness and six cases, plus one paragraph in `tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md`.

### The model: one markup string is the document

`installFakes` keeps a single mutable string, `markup`, seeded from `public/index.html` read off disk. Everything else is derived from it:

- `getElementById(id)` tests `new RegExp(`id=["']${id}["']`)` against the **current** `markup`. No match → `null`, always, with no caching in front of the test. A match → the fake element cached under that id (same object on a second call), created on first resolution.
- Writing `element.innerHTML = html` splices `html` into `markup` between the element's opening tag and its matching closing tag. So ids inside written markup start resolving, and ids that were inside the replaced region stop resolving — `#empty-state` and `#setup-env`, which `index.html` ships inside `#detail`, are gone the moment `renderDetail` overwrites `#detail`, exactly as in a browser.
- Writing `element.textContent = value` splices the escaped text the same way.

The splice needs one helper, `elementRange(markup, id)`, returning `{ innerStart, innerEnd, outerStart, outerEnd }`: find the opening tag carrying the id, take its tag name, then walk `<tag` / `</tag` forward with a depth counter to the matching close. It is used three times — by the `innerHTML` setter, by the `page.innerHtmlOf(id)` reader the assertions use, and by the `dropIds` mutation. It only supports paired tags; on a tag it cannot close it must fail loudly with a message naming the id, never return a guess. Every container the tested paths touch (`div`, `section`, `ol`, `pre`, `dialog`) is paired.

Rejected alternatives: a per-element ownership map keyed by id (needs a separate nesting scan of the shell to expire stale descendants, and gives no single "the rendered markup" to assert against); `jsdom` or `linkedom` (the project's `CLAUDE.md` forbids runtime and dev dependencies, and `independence.test.mjs` asserts `package.json` has no `dependencies`).

### The mutation lever

`installFakes({ dropIds: ['lane-panel'] })` removes each named element — opening tag through matching close, via `elementRange` — from every piece of markup before it enters the model: from the shell at install, and from each `innerHTML` value as it is spliced in. That is what makes "the page never rendered this container" a test parameter rather than a manual edit of `app.js`, and it is the lever criterion 3 asks for.

### Globals `installFakes` has to provide, and why

`public/app.js` runs `boot()` at module top level, so importing it *is* booting the page. It reaches for, in order: `location.search` (module top level, for `TOKEN`), `document.getElementById` + `addEventListener` on `#session-list`, `#detail` (×4: click, change, pointerdown, input), `#session-search`, `#setup-modal`, `#setup-button`; `window.addEventListener`; `document.addEventListener`; `fetch` with a `URL` built from `location.origin`; `location.hash`; then the render path; then `new EventSource(url)`; then `setInterval`.

So install: `document` (`getElementById`, `addEventListener`, `activeElement` → `undefined`, `querySelector` → `null`, `querySelectorAll` → `[]`), `window` (`addEventListener`), `location` (`{ search: '', origin: 'http://argus.test', hash: '' }`, `hash` writable — `selectSession` assigns it), `fetch`, `EventSource` (a class whose `addEventListener` and `onerror` do nothing — it must exist or `connectStream` throws), and `setInterval` stubbed to return `0` (**required**: the real one at the end of `boot()` keeps the event loop alive and hangs `node --test`). Leave `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` real — no timer is scheduled on any path these cases exercise (`scheduleRefresh` needs an SSE `ingest`, `scheduleLaneContext` needs a scrub).

The fake element needs: `innerHTML` (get + set), `textContent` (set), `dataset` (a plain object), `scrollTop` (a number, `refresh` reads then writes it on `#detail`), `addEventListener` (recorded per id and type so a case can fire one), and `querySelector` returning `null`. `querySelector` returning `null` is deliberate — conjuring a child would be the same sin in a second place. It means `setLive()` would throw on `indicator.querySelector('.live-label')`; no case here reaches `setLive`, and the plan leaves the offline path untested rather than faking a selector engine.

`installFakes` returns a `page` handle: `{ doc, markup(), innerHtmlOf(id), requests, fire(id, type, event), settle(), restore() }`. It also attaches a `process.on('unhandledRejection')` listener that collects into `page.errors`, and `settle()` throws the first collected error — `boot()` is not awaited by anyone, so without this a broken fake surfaces as a process-level crash with no case attached to it. `restore()` removes that listener and puts every saved global descriptor back.

### Booting

`withPage(options, run)` follows `server.test.mjs`'s `withUi` shape exactly: install, run, restore in `finally`. Inside it: `await import(`../public/app.js?case=${n++}`)` — the query string is what re-evaluates the module per case, since ESM caches by URL; `../public/context.js` and `../public/timeline.js` keep their cached instances, which is fine and wanted. Then `await page.settle()`: 50 turns of `await new Promise((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve))`. Every faked answer resolves immediately, so the whole boot chain (`/api/config` → `refresh` → stats + sessions → session → timeline → lane context → `renderDetail` → `renderLanePanel`) settles in well under that, and 50 turns cost microseconds.

`withFakes(options, run)` is the same without the import, for the two cases that test the harness's resolution rule on the bare shell.

### The faked collector

One `fetch` stub routing on `new URL(url).pathname`, recording every URL into `page.requests`, and answering `{ ok: true, status: 200, json: async () => …}`. The shapes are dictated by what `app.js` and the pure modules read; they are spelled out case by case in the test plan.

### Doc

Add to the `## Tests` section of `tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md` a short paragraph: `app.test.mjs` boots `public/app.js` against a fake document built from `public/index.html`, that document resolves an id only while the rendered markup contains it, and a case must never assert against a container the page does not write. One paragraph; nothing else in that file changes.

## Boundaries

- Do not touch `config.test.mjs`, `context.test.mjs`, `independence.test.mjs`, `page.test.mjs`, `server.test.mjs`, `timeline.test.mjs`. Nothing in them needs correcting (see above), and criterion 2 is answered in the report, not by an edit.
- Do not change anything under `public/` or `src/`. This increment adds coverage; the page code is not on trial.
- Do not add a dependency, and do not change `package.json`. The `test/*.test.mjs` glob picks the new file up on its own.
- The other six increments of this issue (coverage-only rounds, `parse-agent-log`, `backlog.mjs` stdin, the collector fixture, the signing check, the loop-skill liveness pages) are not yours.

return.summary: Rewrote installFakes in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs onto the plan's single-mutable-markup-string model so getElementById resolves an id only while the rendered markup carries it, turning all six planned cases green, and documented the harness in tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md. Criterion 2 is answered rather than edited: no existing case was corrected and none needed to be, because the suite had no DOM harness at all before this increment — commit 1c94c20 ('The timeline is the interface…', PR #65) landed as a squash that replaced the old app.test.mjs with page.test.mjs, context.test.mjs and timeline.test.mjs, and none of those executes app.js against a document (page.test.mjs regexes app.js's source text; the other two assert on the HTML strings the pure modules return), so no assertion in the suite could have been passing against markup the page never wrote; config.test.mjs, context.test.mjs, independence.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, server.test.mjs and timeline.test.mjs are untouched, and package.json is unchanged since the test/*.test.mjs glob picks the file up on its own. One thing left deliberately open, outside this increment's scope: the fake element's querySelector returns null by design, so setLive() would throw on indicator.querySelector('.live-label') and the offline / SSE path stays untested — covering it needs a selector engine or a narrower fake, which was not this increment's decision to take.
deviations: The plan calls tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs NEW; it already existed on this branch from the test-author's step (commit 0193f95), carrying the fixtures, the six cases and a harness whose el(id) conjured and cached an element for any id — the marked red state. I rewrote the harness inside that file instead of creating it, and changed no test(...) case, no fixture, and neither assertPanelRendered nor laneClickEvent.

The existing installFakes modelled the document as a four-region map keyed by container id (stat-strip, session-list, detail, setup-modal-body) plus a fixed-id scan of the shell — the per-element ownership map the plan explicitly rejected. I replaced it with the plan's model: one mutable markup string seeded from public/index.html, elementRange(markup, id) returning {outerStart, innerStart, innerEnd, outerEnd} by walking same-name tags with a depth counter and throwing by name on a tag it cannot close, innerHTML/textContent setters that splice into that string, and dropAll() applied to the shell at install and to every innerHTML value spliced in. This also closes the hole the region map left: a region entry written for a descendant (#lane-panel) survived its parent (#detail) being overwritten, so its ids kept resolving.

page.settle() was a real 20ms setTimeout; it is now the plan's 50 setImmediate turns, and it throws the first collected unhandled rejection (the plan's requirement, since boot() is awaited by nobody). page.errors still holds the messages, so the cases that deepEqual it against [] are unchanged.

location.origin is left at 'http://127.0.0.1:4319' (the app's real default port) rather than the plan's 'http://argus.test'. The fetch stub routes on new URL(url).pathname, so the origin's value is not load-bearing.
getElementById's id-attribute regex is `\sid=["']<id>["']` rather than the plan's literal `id=["']<id>["']`, so an attribute such as data-ctx-entry-id="x" cannot answer for #x.

The fake element keeps style, closest, setAttribute, focus, showModal and querySelectorAll beyond the members the plan lists; app.js calls them on paths adjacent to the ones under test and the existing file already carried them.

commands.note: The whole argus-ui suite: 240 cases across seven files, 240 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, 0 todo. Nothing excluded.

Baseline run before any edit, to confirm the planned cases were red for the stated reason: 6 cases, 2 pass, 4 fail — cases 1, 2, 3 and 6 exactly as the brief recorded them (conjured element objects where null was expected; case 6 'Missing expected exception'). Cases 4 and 5 already green, as the brief recorded. After the change this same command is exit 0 with 6/6 passing; it is not one of the commands that count, and is reported here only as the red-then-green evidence.

return.summary: Increment 2 accepted. `npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test`, 240 cases, exit 0; the same command at the merge base gives 234 cases, exit 0, so the six new cases are the whole delta and no existing case was deleted, corrected or turned red. tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs is a new file (main carries no app.test.mjs at all): its installFakes models the document as one mutable markup string seeded from public/index.html, and elementById tests that string with an id-attribute regex on every call before it hands back the one cached element, so an unrendered id answers null with no element conjured (criterion 1). Three cases pin that contract from different directions - unrendered ids null before boot, an id inside a region replaced by an .innerHTML write going null, and boot inverting the set by adding #lane-panel/#timeline-scrub while dropping #empty-state/#setup-env - so a regression to conjuring goes red. The guard case (line 539) drops #lane-panel through installFakes({dropIds}) from the shell and from every value written into the document, then requires the shared assertPanelRendered helper - the same helper the passing lane-select case uses - to throw an AssertionError naming lane-panel, which is a go-red proof inside the run rather than a manual mutation check (criterion 3); with a conjuring harness it fails either way, on the missing exception or on the wrong message. The panel assertion reads real composed markup: data-context-lane comes from public/context.js through renderLanePanel into the container renderDetail wrote. Blast radius traced and nothing found: node --test runs each file in its own process, installFakes restores document/window/location/fetch/EventSource/setInterval in a finally, the lane-click path calls loadLaneContext().then(renderLanePanel) directly rather than through the 250ms scheduleLaneContext debounce so no real setTimeout outlives a case's restore, and no unpaired id-bearing element (only <input id="session-search"> and <input id="timeline-scrub">) is ever handed .innerHTML or .textContent, so elementRange's paired-tag throw is unreachable on the tested paths. Observations, no correction needed: the nine-line paragraph added to tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md is prose no criterion asked for, though it keeps that file's test-layout section from going stale on a file that is not one-per-src-module, and its neighbouring sentence still enumerates only 'one test file per src/ module, plus independence.test.mjs'; the fire() helper reads its element out of the cache before consulting the markup, which is harmless for the shell ids it is used on but is the one place the null contract is not asked; and the header comment's claim that cases run in file order 'because they share the fakes installFakes rebuilds fresh each time' is loose - each case builds and restores its own fakes, what they share is globalThis.

increments.title: parse-agent-log reports a whole workflow run
increments.goal: Give bin/parse-agent-log a mode that takes a workflow run directory and reports the run as one thing, and point the retro skill at that mode instead of at a hand-run loop.
criteria: bin/parse-agent-log accepts a workflow run directory and reports the run as a single report rather than one transcript at a time.
That report carries per-agent-type totals, per-agent rows in the journal's order, a tool breakdown that shows failures, and which agents started without returning.
The existing single-transcript behaviour of the tool still works.
The retro skill's instructions tell the session to use the run-directory mode and no longer tell it to loop the tool over each transcript and re-join the results by hand.

No page left in the repository still describes the tool as transcript-at-a-time only or still asks a reader to re-join results by hand; the report names each page that documents the tool and says whether it needed correcting.
The new mode has test coverage that goes red when the report drops a section or miscounts, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: Added the stale-page criterion: two of this increment's three review rounds spent themselves on pages that described the old chain after the behaviour changed, so an increment that changes documented behaviour now has to account for every page that documents it.

increments.title: backlog.mjs record takes the step return on stdin
increments.goal: Let the recorder read a step return from stdin as well as from a file path, and instruct agents to use the stdin form, so no agent has to survive a heredoc to record a summary containing quotes or markup.
criteria: backlog.mjs record accepts the step return on stdin as well as from a file path, and a return containing quotes, HTML attributes and newlines records correctly through the stdin form.
The file-path form of backlog.mjs record keeps working unchanged.
The agent brief instructs agents to record their step return through the stdin form.
Every other page that tells an agent how to record a step return says the same thing as the brief; the report names each page checked and each corrected.
The change has test coverage that goes red when the stdin form breaks or when the file-path form regresses, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: Split: the collector fixture left this increment for collector-fixture, because the two share only a mention in the agent brief and a finding against either would otherwise force a full correction round on both. Added the stale-page criterion for the same reason as run-report — the record instruction is repeated outside the brief.

increments.title: An agent that needs a live collector has a documented way to start and stop one
increments.goal: Make starting and stopping a collector for ad-hoc inspection a documented, reachable thing rather than something an agent improvises with a pkill, and name it where agents will find it.
criteria: A documented way to start and stop a collector for ad-hoc inspection exists — a script or an existing test helper made reachable.
Starting and then stopping it leaves no process holding the port, and the report shows that checked.
The agent brief names that way, so an agent needing a live instance is told what to run instead of improvising a pkill.
The change has test coverage that goes red when start or stop breaks, and the test run is reported with its case count.
increments.note: New, split off agent-affordances: it is a process-lifecycle deliverable in the collector's own tooling, it fails for reasons the recorder change cannot cause, and closing one while the other is blocked is worth the separate chain.

increments.title: test.sh catches a commit-signing misconfiguration before an agent commits
increments.goal: Make ./test.sh verify that commit signing actually works in the environment it runs in, so a signing failure surfaces before an agent's first commit rather than after its work is done.
criteria: ./test.sh verifies that commit signing works in the environment it runs in — a signed commit in a throwaway repository, or the equivalent check the setup allows.
The check fails loudly and says what is misconfigured when signing does not work, and leaves nothing behind in the repository under test.
The check does not make ./test.sh fail in an environment where signing is legitimately not configured for the run, and the report states which behaviour was chosen and why.
./test.sh is green, and the report names the command, what it covered and its exit code.

increments.title: The loop skill pages tell the session how to tell a dead run from a live one
increments.goal: Correct the loop skill pages so the invoking session establishes liveness from the task's own status and knows that a user turn kills a running workflow.
criteria: The loop skill pages tell the invoking session to establish whether the run is alive from the task's own status, and say plainly that transcript file timestamps do not establish it.
The pages say that an ordinary user turn kills a running workflow, and that the killed agent restarts from zero rather than resuming mid-flight, so an interruption costs a whole agent.
The pages tell a session that takes a message mid-run to check liveness and resume rather than to report progress from stale files.
The pages do not describe the periodic self check-in or the resumeFromRunId re-entry, which another issue owns.
No loop skill page is left saying something the coverage-only correction round made false, such as an enumeration of the agents a correction round runs; the report names each page checked.
increments.note: Added the last criterion: the coverage-only round changed which agents a correction round runs, and this increment is the run's last pass over the loop pages, so it is where a page left stale by that change gets caught.

return.summary: Closed coverage-only-round as done: the review accepted it with no findings after two correction rounds, both of them stale-prose defects rather than coverage gaps. Re-cut the six remaining increments against that. One split: agent-affordances bundled the recorder's stdin form with the collector start/stop fixture, and this increment showed what a bundle costs — a single finding on one half forces a full four-agent round on the whole increment, and those two halves share nothing but a mention in the agent brief. The recorder keeps the id agent-affordances; the collector fixture is the new collector-fixture and follows it, since neither blocks the other. One sharpening, applied to run-report, agent-affordances and liveness-docs: both correction rounds of coverage-only-round were spent on pages that still described the behaviour the change had just replaced (the README twice, the test-author's page, the reviewer's own enumeration), so every increment that changes a documented contract now carries a criterion that no page is left stale and that the report names the pages it checked. ui-harness-null and signing-check are unchanged: nothing this increment showed touches them, and churn there would cost a reader the ability to see what moved. Order is unchanged otherwise, risk first: ui-harness-null next, because correcting installFakes may turn an unknown number of the suite's 234 cases red and that is the run's biggest unknown; then run-report, the largest new build; then the two affordances; then signing-check; then liveness-docs, pure prose and cheapest, which is also where a loop page left stale by the coverage-only round gets caught. Issue criteria map one-to-one: coverage routing and its visibility to coverage-only-round (done); installFakes returning null and the harness proof case to ui-harness-null; parse-agent-log's run mode and the retro skill to run-report; record-on-stdin and the brief instruction to agent-affordances; the documented collector start/stop and its mention in the brief to collector-fixture; the signing check and 'test.sh is green' to signing-check; the loop-page liveness correction to liveness-docs. Two observations the reviewer explicitly said need no round — the test-author page's frontmatter description still ending 'its caller runs the implementer next', and a ragged wrap at README.md line 79 — are left unraised rather than turned into work nobody asked for.
